# KONA

> Build your race identity, prepare for race week, explore triathlon machines, people, places and stories, and enter the immersive 3D world when you choose.

An independent, unofficial fan and research project. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Canyon Bicycles GmbH. Canyon and Speedmax are trademarks of their owners.

## Pages
- [KONA · Race the version of yourself](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum/): Build your race identity, prepare for race week, explore triathlon machines, people, places and stories, and enter the immersive 3D world when you choose.
- [Canyon Triathlon Collection · every Speedmax generation, compared](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum/Canyon_Collection.html): Every Canyon Speedmax generation on record, 1999–2027: interactive 3D exhibits, side-by-side specifications, an aero calculator and a sourced archive of the bikes that were never modelled.
- [Studio · Speedmax Museum — build, paint and share a time-trial bike](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum/Studio.html): Every bike in the Speedmax Museum and more, in 3D: paint it, give it a film theme, set the scene, dream it in motion and share it. Canyon generations, named machines and studio designs.
- [Speedmax Nights & History Lane · Canyon Speedmax Museum](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum/Experiences.html): Three night experiences around one Canyon Speedmax (Lava Night, Camp 13 and the Ghost Tunnel) and History Lane, the story from Koblenz in 1985 to Kona. An independent study.
- [Canyon Museum — SpeedMax 3.0 (2007)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum/Speedmax_2007_Museum.html): 3.0 · MY2007 (2007) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.
- [Canyon Museum — Speedmax AL 9.0 (2011)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum/Speedmax_AL_2011_Museum.html): 9.0 · MY2011 (2011) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.
- [Canyon Museum — Speedmax CF 9.0 Pro (2011)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum/Speedmax_CF_2011_Museum.html): 9.0 Pro · MY2011 (2011) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.
- [Canyon Museum — Speedmax CFR AXS (2027)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum/Speedmax_Museum.html): Speedmax CFR AXS (2027) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.
- [Canyon Museum — Speedmax CF SLX 8 Di2 (2027)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum/Speedmax_SLX_Museum.html): Speedmax CF SLX 8 Di2 (2027) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.
- [Canyon Museum — Speedmax Three (2005)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum/Speedmax_Three_2005_Museum.html): Three · MY2005 (2005) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.

## Facts and sources
- Bikes are unofficial procedural Blender reconstructions calibrated against published photographs and geometry; each exhibit lists its sources and known uncertainties.
- Kona titles on a Speedmax (from museum/kona_champions.json): 2015 Jan Frodeno (Speedmax CF SLX); 2016 Jan Frodeno (Speedmax CF SLX); 2017 Patrick Lange (Speedmax CF SLX); 2018 Patrick Lange (Speedmax CF SLX); 2019 Jan Frodeno (Speedmax CF SLX Disc); 2024 Patrick Lange (Speedmax CFR).
- Brand-room studies: Nike Alphafly 3 in Nike Running Lab (Independent reconstructed study from the public specification. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Nike.).
- Photographs are openly licensed (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY / CC BY-SA); authors and licences are shown beside every image.

## Privacy
No accounts, no analytics, no cookies, no tracking by default. The Passport and settings stay in the visitor's own browser (localStorage). An optional email sign-in can back that data up only when the visitor asks.
